title: The replayed areas' alias rows are in _tools/aliases.csv
goal: _tools/aliases.csv holds the alias rows the instance-3 research filed for typescript (ST-j2ctkvl4), zsh (ST-r3tvhelr), Gentoo (ST-oeyfaoee), Kali (ST-2onmjhme), AlmaLinux (ST-za3ew224) and Chef (ST-bamh3apr), each term once over every alias file with an existing canonical reused; rag.py eval passes after the change

run:
import sys;t=[l.strip() for l in open('_tools/aliases.csv',encoding='utf-8')]
need=['tsgo,typescript-go','zshrc,zsh','kalilinux,kali','portage,gentoo','chef infra client,chef-client']
miss=[r for r in need if r not in t]+([] if any(l.startswith('leapp,') for l in t) else ['leapp,'])
print(miss);sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)

rag.py eval passes after the change

notes: Merges the six alias drafts instance 3 filed (ST-j2ctkvl4, ST-r3tvhelr, ST-oeyfaoee, ST-2onmjhme, ST-za3ew224, ST-bamh3apr); their goals list every row in full. A row whose term is already in an alias file, or which turns a lookup eval row, is left out and named in the report, but the check's one row per area stays. Checks that pass before the work: rag.py eval pass before the work and are kept as guards (the change must keep them green); check 0 fails before the work and reads the goal. Each guard check named above as passing on the base passes before the work: it pins behaviour that must stay green (a test selection the work extends, the eval, the lint); the item's failing checks read its goal.
